responsibility: This module implements GCC’s PowerPC/RS6000 target backend and its operating-system and processor-specific subtargets, covering instruction selection, ABI handling, scheduling, options, builtins, and runtime integration for a wide range of PowerPC processors from embedded e500/SPE and Xilinx variants through classic POWER/PowerPC cores, AltiVec/VSX systems, and modern POWER processors. Its core files define the main backend hooks, machine modes, predicates, constraints, options, builtin tables, and master RTL machine descriptions, while the many subsidiary .md families provide both feature-specific lowering for vectors, VSX, SPE, paired-single, decimal floating point, atomics, crypto, and transactional memory and per-CPU pipeline models used by the scheduler. The header and source subtarget layers specialize this backend for major PowerPC environments such as AIX/XCOFF, SysV/ELF, Linux, Darwin, FreeBSD, NetBSD, RTEMS, VxWorks, and Xilinx boards, including ABI defaults, assembler/linker specs, endianness, code model, and secure-PLT or EABI behavior, and the public intrinsic headers expose PowerPC-specific programming interfaces such as AltiVec, SPE, paired-single, HTM, and compatibility wrappers. Overall, this module is the full target-description subsystem that makes GCC generate and tune code correctly for PowerPC-family architectures and their diverse platform ABIs.
